issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) requires a method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) but the template and solution artifacts use inconsistent method names. The template Main references shop.computeMealCost(...), the SealSaloon implementation in the solution defines computeMealCost(Meal) as the static method computing meal cost, while the solution's Main calls shop.calculateTotalPrice(...). This name/signature inconsistency between problem statement, template, and solution (and an internal inconsistency in the solution itself) will confuse students about the expected method name and prevents a straightforward implementation matching the specification and examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Either rename computeMealCost(Meal) in the solution and template to calculateTotalPrice(Meal), and ensure Main calls the same method, or update the problem statement and UML to use computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure the method signature and return type (int) match the specification in all files.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a SealSaloon method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal), but the concrete implementation and example code use a different identifier (computeMealCost). Specifically: the problem statement and solution Main refer to calculateTotalPrice, while SealSaloon implementation defines computeMealCost and the template Main calls computeMealCost. This inconsistent naming across problem text, template, and solution creates confusion for students (which method to implement/call) and can lead to compile-time mismatches when following the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the meal price calculation across all artifacts. Rename computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice in SealSaloon (and update its signature to public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)), and update all call sites in Main and any template code to call calculateTotalPrice. Alternatively, update the problem statement to require computeMealCost — but ensure all template and solution files use the same identifier.
